cues.en: Hello and welcome back.
cues.zh: 你好，歡迎回來。

cues.en: In this tutorial, we're going to have a quick refresher on decision trees.
cues.zh: 這堂快速複習決策樹。

cues.en: All right, so previously we talked about the two types of ensemble models, we learned about the bagging and the boosting classes or categories of models and how they're different,
cues.zh: 先前談了兩種集成模型，Bagging 與 Boosting，以及差異，

cues.en: and now the question is, all right, so we know the principle or the methods of how these ensemble models are created,
cues.zh: 現在問題是，知道如何建立集成模型的原理與方法後，

cues.en: but what models will actually go into doing the hard work, the heavy lifting, the individual models, these 1, 2, 3, etcetera.
cues.zh: 實際做繁重工作的個別模型，這些 1、2、3 等，到底是什麼？

cues.en: What models are we going to use then?
cues.zh: 會使用哪種模型？

cues.en: What models can we use then?
cues.zh: 可以用哪種？

cues.en: Well, the answer is you can use actually any models.
cues.zh: 答案其實是任何模型。

cues.en: You can use linear regressions, logistic regressions, you can use support vector regressions, you can use naive Bayes, whatever you like,
cues.zh: 線性迴歸、邏輯斯迴歸、支援向量迴歸、樸素貝氏，都可以，

cues.en: whatever models you like, you can use.
cues.zh: 任何喜歡的模型。

cues.en: And also, of course, depend if you're doing a regression on classification,
cues.zh: 當然也取決於做迴歸還是分類，

cues.en: regression classification problem, etcetera.
cues.zh: 問題類型等等。

cues.en: So you can use any model, but typically what is used are decision trees.
cues.zh: 可用任何模型，但通常使用決策樹。

cues.en: And the reason decision trees are used is because they're non-linear and they're very simple, very easy to use,
cues.zh: 因為它非線性、非常簡單、容易使用，

cues.en: very easy to implement, very easy to add to these ensemble models, and they get good results.
cues.zh: 容易實作、容易加入集成模型，而且結果好。

cues.en: So let's have a quick refresher on decision trees.
cues.zh: 快速複習決策樹。

cues.en: So, just a quick reminder in the top left that we're talking about those individual models that we're creating, let's say, we're answering the question, how much do customers spend at your store?
cues.zh: 左上角提醒，我們談的是個別模型。假設要回答：顧客在店裡花多少錢？

cues.en: So what a decision tree would do is, for example, once you've created your decision tree, it might look like this.
cues.zh: 建立的決策樹可能像這樣。

cues.en: It might say, okay, if a customer's age is less than 55, yes or no?
cues.zh: 先問：顧客年齡小於 55 嗎？

cues.en: If the answer is no, then they spend on average $153.
cues.zh: 不是，平均花 153 美元。

cues.en: If the answer is yes, then you need to check the next or another variable, another independent variable, what is their travel time to your store?
cues.zh: 是的話，再檢查下一個自變數，到店交通時間。

cues.en: Is the travel time less than one hour?
cues.zh: 小於一小時嗎？

cues.en: If the answer is no, then they spend $87.
cues.zh: 不是，花 87 美元。

cues.en: The answer is yes, then they spend around $20 an average.
cues.zh: 是，平均約 20 美元。

cues.en: So this is an example, very simple, very trivial example of decision tree.
cues.zh: 這是非常簡單的決策樹例子。

cues.en: As you can see, what's basically saying, if, you know, your, per your customer of your store is above a certain age, then they're likely to spend more money.
cues.zh: 基本上說，店裡顧客高於特定年齡，就可能花更多錢。

cues.en: Maybe there might be reasons behind that.
cues.zh: 背後可能有原因。

cues.en: Maybe they have more time to browse or they have more wealth to spend, and so on.
cues.zh: 例如有更多時間逛，或更多財力等等。

cues.en: If their travel time, if that's not the case, then you check travel time.
cues.zh: 若不符合，再看交通時間。

cues.en: If it's less than an hour, then they live close by, so they more come more frequently.
cues.zh: 少於一小時，代表住得近，來得更頻繁。

cues.en: So in one visit they spend $20.
cues.zh: 所以每次花 20 美元。

cues.en: But if the travel time is more than an hour, then they're probably more likely to stock up on the whatever you're selling and buy more.
cues.zh: 超過一小時，可能更想囤貨，多買一些。

cues.en: So that's an example of a decision tree, how it goes through the logic.
cues.zh: 這是決策樹邏輯的例子。

cues.en: It's a very trivial example, it's only got two levels.
cues.zh: 非常簡單，只有兩層。

cues.en: So this is level one over here.
cues.zh: 這裡第一層。

cues.en: Then this is like one branch.
cues.zh: 這是一個分支。

cues.en: Then this is another.
cues.zh: 這是另一個。

cues.en: These are subbranches here.
cues.zh: 這些是子分支。

cues.en: So it's got these three, these are called terminal leaves.
cues.zh: 這三個叫做終端葉節點。

cues.en: And of course, it can be much deeper, it can be 10, it can be more levels, as much as you like.
cues.zh: 當然可以深得多，10 層或更多，任你選。

cues.en: And the other thing is that this decision tree has two variables.
cues.zh: 另外，這棵樹有兩個變數。

cues.en: So it's got age and travel time, as an example.
cues.zh: 年齡與交通時間。

cues.en: Your dataset might have lots and lots of independent variables, and therefore, your decision tree will be combining many of them.
cues.zh: 資料集可能有非常多自變數，決策樹會組合其中很多個。

cues.en: But in our case, we're going to, in the upcoming trials, we're going to be looking mostly at decision trees with just one variable.
cues.zh: 但接下來教學，主要會看只有一個變數的樹。

cues.en: And that is to make things simpler and for illustration purposes.
cues.zh: 為了簡單與說明。

cues.en: And then in the practical tutorials, of course, you'll be looking at more variables again.
cues.zh: 實作當然又會使用更多變數。

cues.en: All right, I look forward to seeing you in the upcoming tutorials.
cues.zh: 期待接下來見。

cues.en: And until then, enjoy machine learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，享受機器學習的樂趣吧。
